phasing_details.phase_detail: It is only a small dormer to be finished in one week if available labours obtained.

subdivision_of_building:
The existing skylights on the rear roof to the balcony on the first floor rear bedroom which stands on the flat roof as part of the rear roof intended to be replaced with a timber structured dormer to cover the flat roof where owing to defective on original design of the flat roof where using as the floor of the balcony that the non weather proof materials under the service area of the flat roof obsoleted, deteriorated and collapsed leading rain water leaking into the house living area in the past wet raining exceptional season during the past few months exaggerated the leaking situation. The surrounding two side walls and the front low wall ill designed and non water proof with high difficulties in repairing without the whole rear roof replaced. 

The house is a leasholder property and the rear roof belongs in theory to the freeholder who reluctant to make good the leakage. Upon this application of development granted, we will apply consent from the freeholder to proceed the dormer work. This new dormer structure could cover the open area of the flat roof and water proof to the area saving complicated work on the rear roof and the surrounding walls where totally enclosed by the dormer for the weather issues.

The dormer would NOT increase the view angle of the house and in fact more restrictive to the area at the balcony which now enclosed completely insider the dormer and the view becomes only to the rear as the skylight approved under APPLICATION NUMBER: 2025/2116 where both would not affect privacy to all the neighbor's houses.

The new dormer would not increase the size of the property and only bringing the outside approximately 4 square meters into insider covered and the total usable area would be the same. Those 4 square meters are only a very small area and nothing to be big.
Also it would not use additional areas of the land in question.
It is in the rear and not at front with nothing near to the highway in the area.
The house is not in the national or conservation parks areas at all.
In fact the development comprises with all conditions of a class A development in my previouse application  PP-14677988 APPLICATION NUMBER: 2026/0472 and this application just to make good the satisfaction of the conditions required under the laws as supplement to the aforementioned application under class A development. Please refer to the details of development mentioned in the above application form and statement submitted now enclosed.
The material using would be matching with the existing materials to the roof and houses. Windows will face exactly the same direction to the existing skylights at the balcony to be replaced.
The dormer would not create or look like a full additional floor. 
The dormer would not be in the view of the public at all. It is facing the rear garden of the house and the rear side of the house does not have any other houses at all. This has been confirmed in the said APPLICATION NUMBER: 2025/2116 during the application progress.
description:
Reasonable Exception Statement (RES)
London Plan Guidance Planning Fire Safety Strategy Policy D.12 Site:
At 13 Falmouth Walk, SW15 5DY
I Kai SO is the occupant/owner of the erection of a window dormer to the existing
balcony windows area to avoid water leakage into the house from the existing flat
roof/balcony floor area.
Description of development: Proposed erection of a dormer windows to the
existing balcony on the first floor to stop the water leakage from the existing flat
roof of the balcony into the living room at the ground floor beneath it.
The current fire safety measures are appropriate and will not be adversely
a4ected by the existing development.
1. Information on space provisions for fire appliances and assembly points -
There is not planed to obscure the suitable positioned unobstructed outside
space for Fire Appliance. All the existing fire precaution equipment and
escape way in the house and outside the building on the common area and
main road or in very close proximity to meet hose length criteria. Evacuation
assembly point will be in the same location (RES).
2. Information on passive and active safety measures -
The building has been designed to incorporate features to reduce the risk to life.
Passive and Active protection in accordance with current Building Regulations
(RES).
3. Information and data on construction products and materials -
New building work will be constructed to minimise the risk of fire spread to
the surrounding areas in accordance with current Building Regulations.
Exterior material roof of façade has already been designed in accordance
with current Building Regulations (RES).
4. Information on means of escape and evacuation strategy -
The project provides a suitable and convenient means of escape and
associated evacuation strategy. Occupants will be able to escape via
windows and/ or fire resistance compartment walls and fire doors directly to
open area. (RES) There are already su4icient to robust strategy for evacuation
of escape in the event of a fire which will likely be triggered by warning mains
operated interlinked smoke and fire alarms.(RES)
5. Information on access and equipment for firefighting –
The building has a suitable access and equipment for fire-fighting is not
required on this project and will not be provided apart from the local fire
brigade in an emergency situation. Estate management has already su4icient
planning to cater any fire and smoke events upon occurred. An adequate
firefighting water supply always be provided by the Fire Appliances (RES).
All of the above information is based on the fact that the building is NOT a
MAJOR DEVELOPMENT and it is being established that NO net impact on
existing Fire Safety Provisions. The project site and all works will comply with
the minimum Fire Safety Standards of the national Building Regulations
requirements.
